weekend_summary: Miami was the first major development flashpoint of the season and the first weekend under the post-Suzuka energy-management refinements. McLaren converted Sprint pole into a one-two, but Antonelli took Grand Prix pole and won Sunday after a chaotic race with repeated lead changes, an early Safety Car and a successful Mercedes undercut on Norris. The weekend showed the field closing around Mercedes without removing the Silver Arrows from the top step.

SQ.summary: Norris took Sprint pole ahead of Antonelli and Piastri, giving McLaren its clearest single-lap result of the opening phase.

key_moments.text: Norris started the Sprint from pole.

S.summary: Norris controlled the Sprint ahead of Piastri for a McLaren one-two, with Leclerc third.

key_moments.text: Norris won the 19-lap Sprint from Piastri and Leclerc.
Antonelli dropped from the front row and was later penalised for track limits.

Q.summary: Antonelli responded by taking Grand Prix pole, ahead of Verstappen, Leclerc and Norris.

key_moments.text: Antonelli set a 1:27.798 to take pole ahead of Verstappen.

R.summary: Antonelli won from Norris and Piastri after a race with multiple leaders, an early Safety Car and a decisive Mercedes undercut.

key_moments.text: Antonelli, Verstappen and Leclerc converged at Turn 1; Verstappen later spun and dropped back.
Separate incidents for Gasly and Hadjar brought out the Safety Car early.
Mercedes undercut Norris with Antonelli, putting the teenager onto fresh tyres and into control of the race.
Antonelli managed late gearbox/downshift concerns while holding Norris off to win.

performance_snapshot.status: hydrate at query time from committed LatentLap session data

ANT.name: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
ANT.summary: Antonelli paired Grand Prix pole with his third straight win, but Sunday required recovery after another imperfect first corner and sustained pressure from Norris.

details.text: Mercedes' undercut was central to turning his fresh-tyre pace into track position.

NOR.name: Lando Norris
NOR.summary: Norris won the Sprint and then pushed Antonelli closely in the Grand Prix, making Miami the clearest proof to that point that McLaren had moved into genuine win contention.

details.text: McLaren's large upgrade package coincided with the step, but the dossier does not isolate how many tenths came from the hardware itself.

PIA.name: Oscar Piastri
PIA.summary: Piastri completed the Sprint one-two and finished third in the Grand Prix, giving McLaren two cars consistently near the front across both races.

details.text: The result supports a team-level step rather than a one-driver anomaly.

VER.name: Max Verstappen
VER.summary: Verstappen qualified on the front row after Red Bull's major update, but a spin in the Grand Prix damaged his track position and made the final result less representative of qualifying potential.

details.text: F1 technical analysis described the Miami package as a very major project linked with Red Bull's competitive turnaround.

Mercedes.summary: Mercedes retained the Grand Prix victory even as the field compressed, relying on Antonelli's pace plus a successful undercut.

details.text: Miami was the first weekend where the margin looked materially less comfortable than the opening rounds.

McLaren.summary: McLaren was transformed into a direct win threat across the Sprint and Grand Prix, with Norris and Piastri both consistently at the front.

details.text: The large package worked in the same weekend as the performance jump, but LatentLap should still avoid component-level causal attribution.

Red Bull.summary: Red Bull's major package substantially changed the car and Verstappen qualified P2, but race execution was compromised by the spin.

details.text: F1 technical reporting explicitly described the package as a major turnaround point.

Ferrari.summary: Ferrari remained in the lead fight early and Leclerc qualified third, but the team did not match McLaren/Mercedes over the full race.

details.text: Ferrari also brought the largest item count in its early-season development push.

strategy_and_conditions.text: The Sprint format limited practice time while several teams introduced major packages.
The Grand Prix featured an early Safety Car and repeated lead changes before the strategy sequence settled.
Regulation refinements agreed after the opening races reduced maximum qualifying recharge to 7MJ and increased peak superclip power, with changes applied from Miami.

performance_interpretation.text: McLaren's Sprint one-two and GP double podium show a genuine team-level competitive step; the exact share attributable to the upgrade package versus circuit/setup cannot be isolated from the public data.
Antonelli's GP win remained representative of Mercedes front-running pace, but the undercut was a meaningful execution factor.

prediction_review.overall_assessment: A genuine pre-race Miami forecast exists in the repository, but it predates the newer four-file Q/R/SQ/S prediction format. Keep it as a legacy original forecast and evaluate it from the saved prediction/actual artifacts rather than reconstructing a modern forecast retrospectively.

known_exceptions.text: Miami uses the legacy blended prediction schema, so it is not directly comparable field-for-field with the later Netherlands/Italy prediction files.

knowledge_limits.text: Actual ERS deployment and battery state are not public; LatentLap's energy-management signals remain inferred, not measured.
Race-session harvest ratios are not used as reliable comparative evidence because representative laps differ in fuel, compound and track evolution.
Stint pace trends are fitted lap-time slopes over filtered green-flag laps, not direct tyre-degradation measurements; fuel burn, traffic, track evolution and driver management can contribute.
The presence of a new component at a weekend does not prove it caused an observed pace change. Upgrade effects are only attributed where reviewed reporting explicitly supports an effect.
